paragraphs: Three fostering services list Derby as an area they cover, and all three are shown above: Derby City Council's own fostering service and two independent agencies. Fostering for the council means caring for children from the city with the council's social workers behind you; an agency assesses, approves and supports its own carers and takes children councils ask it to place.

During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2026 the council said more carers were urgently needed so that every child could be matched with a home that suits them. One scheme it has promoted is Fostering Plus, for young people moving from residential care into a family, who are likely to have complex needs and may have moved several times. The council describes it as a full-time, self-employed role, with a supervising social worker, therapeutic support built around the young person, out-of-hours help in the evenings and at weekends, training in attachment and therapeutic parenting, and 28 days of paid respite a year.

The council's allowance booklet for 2024-25 sets weekly allowances for each child from £170 for children up to four to £274.56 for 16 to 18-year-olds, with a separate skills payment in four bands from £80 to £230 a week, extra payments for birthdays, festivals and holidays, and a £500 weekly skills payment on top of the child's allowances for Fostering Plus. Parent and child placements were paid £700 a week. These were the rates for 2024-25, so ask the council for this year's figures.
Speak to the council and the agencies above and compare training, support and pay before you decide. The Derbyshire and Leicester pages list more services nearby.
